stem.text: Let f be the function defined by \( f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{- x^{2} + 5 x - 4}{x - 1}, & x \ne 1 \\ 0, & x = 1 \end{cases} \). Determine whether f is continuous at \( x = 1 \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: f is not continuous at \( x = 1 \), because the limit of f(x) there is 3 while f(1) = 0.

worked_solution.text: The function value at the boundary is \( f(1) = 0 \), from the second line of the rule.
worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the function at the input

worked_solution.text: For \( x \ne 1 \) the quotient simplifies to \( 4 - x \), so \( \lim_{x \to 1} f(x) = 3 \) from both sides.
The limit exists and equals 3, but \( f(1) = 0 \), so the limit does not equal the function value and f is not continuous at \( x = 1 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: the limit must equal the function value

options.label: f is not continuous at \( x = 1 \), because the quotient gives 0/0 at \( x = 1 \), so f(1) is undefined.
options.derivation: x = 1 substituted into the quotient, which applies only for x not equal to 1, giving 0/0

options.label: f is continuous at \( x = 1 \), because the limits from the left and from the right are both 3.
options.derivation: continuity concluded from the agreement of the one sided limits, with the function value never compared
